q1_issues.issue: (Theme sk_reputation_1 (Member sk_lawyer_1 ambulance_chaser)) hangs a thematic role and a sealed proposition off an ordinary entity witness; roles attach to event witnesses, and Theme-sealing is licensed only for an attitude / embedded-question EVENT, never for a content noun.

(Inheritance ambulance_chaser (can chase)) fires the agent-nominalization rule although its second required test fails — 'an ambulance chaser is one who chases ambulances' is not true by definition — so the compound should have stayed a plain kind.
(Chase ambulance_chaser ambulance) asserts the literal kind-relation of a non-compositional idiom, the same error the section's spill_the_beans example forbids (no ambulances are being chased).

q2_gaps: a content noun taking an 'of'-gerund complement clause ('has the reputation of being an ambulance chaser'): the Propositional attitudes section is restricted to a thought / speech VERB with a finite that-clause, so nothing specifies how to attach an unasserted proposition to a noun such as 'reputation' (and 'reputation' is a hearsay report, so the proposition must not be asserted)
notes: The have-event (Holder / Theme) and the decision not to assert that the lawyer really IS an ambulance chaser are both right. Notably the parse correctly withheld the compound genus (Inheritance ambulance_chaser chaser) as non-compositional — which is precisely why the two nominalization atoms should have been withheld as well.
